title: Street-tree root subsidence claims: council has no seasonal evidence to rebut the insurer
problem: A home insurer's adjuster blames a council street tree for cracking on shrinkable clay and demands felling or damages; councils have been ordered to pay ~£150k+ on single claims (Robbins v Bexley) and ALARM put council subsidence costs at ~£200m/yr, mostly tree-related. The only evidence is insurer-commissioned manual level monitoring every ~6-8 weeks for 12+ months, so the council cannot show whether movement tracks soil drying near the tree or something else (drains, leaks).
who_suffers: Council tree officers and insurance/claims teams fighting claims they cannot evidence; residents whose healthy street trees get felled defensively
buyer: Council Insurance & Risk Manager (with Arboricultural/Tree Manager); alternatively home-insurer subsidence claims managers
industry: Local authority street-tree stock on shrinkable clay (London and South-East boroughs)
sector: Local councils – parks, highways, street assets
current_workaround: Insurer-appointed engineers do precise-level/crack monitoring visits every ~2 months; root ID lab tests; council arborist site visits; pre-emptive felling or root barriers
sensor_concept: Per-claim kit leased for 12-18 months: wall-mounted tilt + crack-width displacement sensor on the claimant's building plus 2-3 capacitive soil-moisture probes at 1-2 m depth near the tree; LoRaWAN/NB-IoT, 5-yr battery; auto report correlating seasonal movement with soil-moisture deficit for Joint Mitigation Protocol disputes
notes: Strong c1 (sourced six-figure claims + ALARM aggregate), c3 (paid level-monitoring visits), c6 (loss adjusters/arboricultural consultants already on site); risk on c2 (per-claim, not per-site cadence)

title: Council park lakes under the Reservoirs Act: weekly walk-out to read the gauge board for the statutory s11 record
problem: Councils owning large raised reservoirs (≥25,000 m3: park lakes, former mill ponds, flood storage) must keep records of water level and spillway flow at intervals set by their Supervising Engineer; failing to keep them is an offence under Reservoirs Act 1975 s11 that the EA reviews and can caution/prosecute. Staff walk out weekly (and after heavy rain) to read gauge boards and V-notch seepage weirs; gaps get flagged in the Supervising Engineer's annual statement.
who_suffers: Parks staff doing the readings; the council's nominated reservoir representative who signs off compliance
buyer: Parks & Open Spaces Manager / council Flood Risk Manager acting for the reservoir undertaker
industry: Council-owned large raised reservoirs and park lakes in England and Wales
sector: Local councils – parks, highways, street assets
current_workaround: Manual weekly gauge-board readings onto paper forms; ad-hoc storm visits; occasional expensive SCADA telemetry from engineering consultancies
sensor_concept: Solar/battery radar or ultrasonic level sensor over the spillway crest plus pressure transducer in the lake, optional seepage-weir level; NB-IoT/LTE-M; automatic s11-format record, high-level and rapid-drawdown alerts to the Supervising Engineer and on-call officer
notes: Strong c4 (statutory record duty + offence), c2 (weekly readings), c3, c6 (Supervising Engineers/panel engineers direct the instrumentation); also sells to private estates, angling clubs, canal-side owners

title: Culvert trash screens block in a storm and flood homes; councils still drive round to look
problem: Debris blinds council-owned culvert trash screens during storms, backing water into homes and roads; Southend spent ~£15k and four days clearing one culvert blockage. Councils run weekly plus post-rainfall inspection rounds; existing telemetry is costly (Fife quoted ~£3.4k install + ~£1.3k/yr for one screen; Carmarthenshire ~£40k for a network) so most screens remain unmonitored.
who_suffers: Drainage engineers and on-call crews; residents flooded downstream
buyer: Flood Risk / Land Drainage Manager at the Lead Local Flood Authority
industry: Council-maintained culvert trash screens and ordinary watercourses
sector: Local councils – parks, highways, street assets
current_workaround: Weekly inspection rounds plus storm call-outs; a few high-risk screens with £3k+ telemetry; CCTV at some
sensor_concept: Pair of ultrasonic/radar level sensors upstream and downstream of the screen (head-loss = blockage), LoRaWAN or NB-IoT, solar/battery; alerts on differential head rising with rainfall; inspection-replacement log and clearance verification
notes: Strong c3 (quantified telemetry & inspection costs), c2 (weekly inspections), c7 (priced incumbents at £3k+ prove WTP and leave a sub-£500 gap); c4 moderate (FWMA 2010/Land Drainage Act duties)

title: Newly planted street trees die of drought in years 1-3 while watering contractors bill for weekly visits
problem: Councils planting thousands of trees (often grant-funded, e.g. UTCF paid ~£151-£189 per tree per year for 3 years of establishment and excluded replacements) lose a share in dry summers; each replacement costs ~£500-£1,500 in stock, pit and labour. Watering contractors are paid per visit whether or not soil is dry, and the council cannot verify visits happened.
who_suffers: Tree officers answering for dead trees; parks contract managers
buyer: Council Tree Officer / Urban Forest Manager / Parks Contract Manager
industry: Local authority urban tree planting and 3-year establishment programmes
sector: Local councils – parks, highways, street assets
current_workaround: Fixed weekly watering rounds by contractor bowsers, watering bags, end-of-season dead-tree surveys and paid replacements
sensor_concept: Capacitive soil-moisture probe at two depths in the tree pit plus temperature, LoRaWAN, 3-yr battery; daily 'needs water' route list, moisture-spike verification that each contractor visit happened, establishment report for grant/funder
notes: c2 (weekly rounds), c3 (paid contractor visits), c6 (landscape/establishment contractors), c9 (3-yr establishment period subscription); c4 relies on grant establishment conditions

title: Hit-and-run strikes on lighting columns and signal poles: no impact timestamp, so the council eats the repair bill
problem: Vehicles knock down lighting columns, illuminated bollards and traffic-signal poles; one Perth junction strike cost ~£13k, columns typically ~£2-5k. Councils (or PFI lighting contractors) recover costs only if police identify the driver, otherwise the taxpayer pays; a damaged column left leaning is also a liability (one council was ordered to pay ~£80k after a falling lamppost injured a man).
who_suffers: Street lighting and traffic-signal teams; council insurance recovery officers
buyer: Street Lighting Manager / PFI lighting contract manager / council Insurance Recovery Officer
industry: Highway street lighting, illuminated street furniture and traffic signal assets
sector: Local councils – parks, highways, street assets
current_workaround: Night scouting patrols, public fault reports, police reports, manual recharge attempts; most unknown-driver damage written off
sensor_concept: Epoxied shock + tilt tag inside the column door or signal pole base, NB-IoT/LTE-M, 10-yr battery; impact time, severity and lean angle; instant 'knocked down/leaning' alert and an evidence pack (time + location) to match ANPR/CCTV for insurer recovery
notes: c1 (sourced £2-13k per strike), c2 (large councils log many strikes a year), c6 (PFI/term lighting contractors already do night scouting & structural testing); c4 weaker — mainly recovery, some smart-lighting CMS nodes already have tilt

title: Utility roadworks: barriers left on site after the job ends trigger s74 overrun charges up to £10k/day
problem: Under NRSWA s74, overrunning works on traffic-sensitive streets are charged up to £5k/day for the first 3 days then £10k/day; councils have levied ~£850k in months (Shropshire) and ~£483k in a year (Cambridgeshire 2024-25). Disputes hinge on when the site was really cleared, and contractors are charged when signs/barriers are left behind after the work is finished (Great Yarmouth reported huge delays from uncollected signs).
who_suffers: Utility streetworks coordinators and their traffic-management subcontractors; councils' streetworks inspectors arguing about dates
buyer: Utility Streetworks Manager / contractor Traffic Management Manager (or council Network/Streetworks Manager)
industry: Utility and contractor roadworks on local authority highways
sector: Local councils – parks, highways, street assets
current_workaround: Gang-leader phone photos, Street Manager status updates typed later, inspectors' site visits, appeals and negotiation over charges
sensor_concept: GPS + motion tracker clipped into barrier/sign feet, LTE-M, multi-year battery; geofenced 'site live/cleared' timestamps auto-matched to the Street Manager permit; overnight 'signing present' proof for Red Book compliance
notes: c1 (statutory per-day charges, sourced council totals), c2 (daily), c4 (NRSWA s74 + FPNs), c6 (barrier/traffic-management hire firms deliver and collect daily)

title: Precautionary gritting runs (~£2-2.5k each) triggered by a handful of £20k road weather stations that miss local cold spots
problem: Duty officers decide nightly Oct-Apr whether to salt; each precautionary run costs ~£2,028 (West Berkshire) to ~£2,500 (Swindon). Councils own only a few road weather stations (~£16-23k each), so known cold spots (bridges, shaded hills) either drive whole-route runs or are missed, exposing the council to Highways Act s41(1A) ice claims.
who_suffers: Winter duty officers making blind decisions at 3am; gritter crews; drivers
buyer: Winter Service Manager / Highways Network Manager
industry: Local highway authority winter service
sector: Local councils – parks, highways, street assets
current_workaround: Forecast provider contract plus sparse road weather stations; patrols of cold spots; conservative over-salting
sensor_concept: Non-contact IR road-surface thermometer + air temp/RH (dew point) mounted on lamp columns at cold spots, NB-IoT/LoRaWAN, battery/solar; feeds the council's forecast provider and logs each decision for the winter service record
notes: c1 (sourced per-run costs), c2 (daily decisions all winter), c4 (s41(1A) duty + Well-managed Highway Infrastructure code records), c6 (MetDesk/Vaisala/DTN already sell to every council), c7 (£20k incumbents)

title: Hidden supply-pipe leaks at parks, cemeteries and allotments run for months behind estimated water bills
problem: Since the 2017 non-household water market, councils pay for leaks on their side of remote meters at parks, cemeteries, allotments and sports pavilions; meters sit in flooded chambers, are rarely read and bills are estimated, so a buried leak can run for months and land as a ~£5-20k catch-up bill, and retailer leak allowances need evidence of prompt repair.
who_suffers: Parks facilities staff and council energy & water teams
buyer: Council Energy & Water Manager / Parks Facilities Manager
industry: Council parks, cemeteries, allotments and sports pavilions water supplies
sector: Local councils – parks, highways, street assets
current_workaround: Occasional manual meter reads, waiting for bills, leak detection contractor once a leak is suspected
sensor_concept: Optical/magnetic pulse reader clipped to the existing meter in the chamber, NB-IoT (deep coverage), 10-yr battery; night-flow analysis and continuous-flow alerts; monthly read file for the retailer and leak-allowance evidence
notes: c1 (leak bills), c3 (manual reads/estimates), c6 (water retailers and water-management brokers already bundle AMR); c7 risk — AMR loggers exist for offices, niche is remote unpowered chambers

title: Pothole injury claims: council can't prove when the defect appeared to win the s58 defence
problem: Councils defend pothole and trip claims under Highways Act s58 by showing a reasonable inspection regime and that the defect wasn't there at the last inspection; claims each cost ~£hundreds (vehicle damage) to ~£10k+ (cyclist injury) plus handling. Driven safety inspections happen monthly-to-yearly by road category, so between inspections there is no record of when a defect formed.
who_suffers: Highway inspectors and council insurance/claims handlers
buyer: Highways Asset Manager / Highways Claims & Insurance Manager
industry: Local highway authority road and footway safety inspection
sector: Local councils – parks, highways, street assets
current_workaround: Scheduled driven safety inspections, public reports via FixMyStreet, camera-AI surveys bought periodically
sensor_concept: Accelerometer + GNSS tag bolted to council refuse/fleet vehicles that already drive every street weekly, LTE-M; detects jolt signatures, geotags emerging defects and creates a dated 'coverage and jolt' evidence trail for s58 defence and risk-based inspection
notes: c2 (daily data), c4 (s58 + Well-managed Highway Infrastructure code), c1 (claim volumes), c6 (fleet telematics providers); c7 risk — camera-AI incumbents (Gaist, RoadAI) exist but are pricier

title: Ward window restrictors forced, broken or missing between audits: patient falls and HSE prosecutions
problem: Patients fall from hospital windows where restrictors were missing, set wrong or defeated; HSE prosecutions followed (e.g. Walsall ~£80k fine, Royal United Hospitals Bath £200k after an incomplete restrictor maintenance system, NHS Lothian £220k after two deaths, Medway £42k). Estates teams check thousands of restrictors by hand on audit cycles, so a broken one can go unnoticed for months.
who_suffers: Patients at risk (dementia, delirium, mental health); estates teams and ward managers
buyer: Head of Estates / Trust Health & Safety Manager
industry: NHS acute and mental-health hospital wards with openable windows
current_workaround: Periodic manual restrictor audits and PPM, incident-driven checks, ward staff reports
sensor_concept: Magnet + hall-effect/accelerometer tag on the sash measuring opening beyond 100 mm or restrictor cable released; LoRaWAN to a cellular gateway (no trust IT); instant estates alert, audit log replacing manual checks
notes: Strong c1 + c4 (multiple sourced HSE fines, HSE guidance on falls from windows in health/social care), c2 (recurring audits), c8 (cheap reed/hall sensors); channel via window maintenance/FM contractors

title: Airborne-isolation rooms lose negative pressure silently; nurses log a dial gauge once a day
problem: Negative-pressure isolation rooms (TB, measles, COVID) and positive-pressure neutropenic rooms only protect if the pressure cascade holds; doors propped, loaded filters or fan faults make rooms fail between the daily nurse reading of a magnehelic gauge and annual HTM 03-01 verification. A failed room means cross-infection risk, bay closures and outbreak costs.
who_suffers: Infection prevention teams, ward nurses doing daily checks, patients
buyer: Estates Ventilation Authorised Person / Infection Prevention & Control Lead
industry: NHS isolation rooms and specialised ventilation in older buildings without BMS alarms
current_workaround: Daily nurse reading of gauge (paper log), smoke/tissue tests, annual verification by ventilation contractors
sensor_concept: MEMS differential-pressure sensor (±125 Pa) + door contact, LoRaWAN to cellular gateway; continuous log, alert when pressure out of range for >5 min with door closed, automatic daily record replacing nurse check
notes: c2 (daily mandated checks), c4 (HTM 03-01/HBN 04-01 Supplement 1), c3 (nurse time + verification contractors), c8 (Sensirion-class DP sensor ~£20); c1 needs outbreak cost sourcing

title: Thousands of Type 3 TMVs serviced on fixed cycles because nobody can prove they're still mixing correctly
problem: HTM 04-01 requires Type 3 thermostatic mixing valves in healthcare, with in-service testing and servicing (D08 schedule); hospitals pay water-hygiene contractors per valve per visit across thousands of outlets, yet failing TMVs still deliver scalding water (scalding was historically an NHS 'Never Event') or run cold enough to grow Legionella.
who_suffers: Estates water-safety teams; patients at scald risk
buyer: Water Safety Responsible Person / Head of Estates Compliance
industry: NHS hospital domestic hot water outlets with TMVs
current_workaround: Contracted TMV in-service tests and annual/6-monthly servicing; paper/CAFM logs
sensor_concept: Clamp-on thermistor pair on mixed outlet and hot inlet pipes detecting each use and its peak mixed temperature, LoRaWAN, 5-yr battery; drift >44°C or fail-safe failure alerts; evidence to move servicing to risk-based intervals
notes: c3 (tendered TMV servicing contracts), c4 (HTM 04-01 + D08), c6 (water-hygiene contractors), c2 (continuous); c7 risk — legionella temperature monitoring incumbents exist

title: Point-of-use water filters in neonatal/ICU units left on past expiry
problem: Augmented-care units fit point-of-use filters on taps and showers to control Pseudomonas (guidance tightened after the 2012 Belfast neonatal deaths); filters expire after ~1-3 months. Audits find expired, missing or wrongly fitted filters, and trusts over-replace early 'to be safe', spending heavily on consumables.
who_suffers: Infection prevention and estates water teams; vulnerable neonatal/ICU patients
buyer: Water Safety Group chair / Estates Water Manager / IPC Lead
industry: NHS augmented-care units (neonatal, ICU, haematology, burns)
current_workaround: Date stickers on filters, paper change logs, scheduled change rounds by supplier or estates
sensor_concept: Clip-on tag on filter housing with NFC install-date pairing and flow-event detection (temperature/vibration), LoRaWAN; usage- and date-based change countdown, missing-filter detection, audit export for the Water Safety Group
notes: c9 (consumable-linked subscription), c4 (HTM 04-01 Part B/C), c2 (monthly change cycle), c6 (filter suppliers' reps already visit to change filters)

title: Rented dynamic air mattresses left on hire after discharge, idling in corridors
problem: Trusts rent dynamic pressure-relief mattresses by the day; units stay on hire after patients go home, sit in cupboards or go missing, and one trust reported ~£98k/yr rental spend while an audit elsewhere found ~83% over-prescribed (both via supplier case studies). Nobody can see which units are actually in use.
who_suffers: Tissue viability nurses, equipment library staff, finance
buyer: Medical Equipment Library Manager / Tissue Viability Lead / Procurement Manager
industry: NHS acute and community hospital rental of dynamic mattresses
current_workaround: Manual equipment hunts, ward off-hire phone calls, supplier rental statements reconciled monthly
sensor_concept: Plug-through current sensor on the pump's mains lead (in use vs idle) + accelerometer + BLE ward beacon/LoRaWAN location, cellular gateway; daily 'idle >24h, off-hire now' list; external power monitoring only, not touching therapy function
notes: c1 (rental spend), c2 (daily), c3 (manual hunts), c6 (rental suppliers could bundle as managed service); c1 sources are vendor-heavy so needs FOI corroboration

title: Blood units returned unused from theatre are binned because nobody can prove they stayed cold
problem: Red cell units issued to theatres/wards in transport boxes must stay within temperature limits; under typical '30-minute rule' policies, units out of controlled storage too long are discarded. Each red cell unit costs ~£150, wastage is tracked nationally, and the Blood Safety and Quality Regulations 2005 require traceability with MHRA inspections.
who_suffers: Transfusion laboratory staff and theatre teams; blood stock budgets
buyer: Transfusion Laboratory Manager / Hospital Transfusion Team
industry: NHS hospital transfusion services and blood transport boxes
current_workaround: Paper time-out records, conservative discard of returned units, validated transport boxes with no live data
sensor_concept: Temperature + lid-open logger inside each blood transport box, BLE handshake to lab gateway on return, cellular fallback; per-unit time-temperature record so compliant units go back into stock
notes: c1 (per-unit value x waste volume), c4 (BSQR 2005 + MHRA inspections), c2 (daily), c9 (traceability records); c8 must avoid being classed as a medical device

title: Ward fire doors wedged open on busy wards: fire enforcement risk and failed fire-door audits
problem: Ward and cross-corridor fire doors get wedged open for trolley traffic; under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order and HTM 05-03, trusts must keep compartmentation intact, and fire & rescue services can issue enforcement notices. Fire-door audits are periodic and wedging happens between them.
who_suffers: Fire safety advisers, estates, ward managers, patients who cannot self-evacuate
buyer: Trust Fire Safety Manager / Head of Estates
industry: NHS acute hospital ward compartmentation
current_workaround: Fire safety walkrounds, quarterly fire-door inspections, retrofitting powered hold-open devices on some doors
sensor_concept: Door contact + accelerometer on the leaf distinguishing 'held open without a hold-open device' for >N minutes; LoRaWAN to cellular gateway; alerts and heat-map report showing chronic doors (where to fit hold-opens)
notes: c4 (FSO + HTM 05-03), c2 (daily), c3 (walkrounds); research needed on NHS-specific enforcement notices for c1/c10

title: Mobile patient hoists can't be found when the LOLER inspector visits
problem: LOLER requires thorough examination of equipment for lifting people every 6 months; engineering inspectors list mobile hoists as 'not seen', leaving them overdue (unusable or uninsured) and triggering revisit charges, while some overdue hoists stay in use.
who_suffers: EBME/estates teams, ward staff searching for hoists, insurer inspectors
buyer: EBME Manager / Medical Devices Safety Officer
industry: NHS and private hospital mobile hoist and lifting-equipment fleets
current_workaround: Asset registers, ward-by-ward searches before inspection, revisit bookings with the inspection body
sensor_concept: Rugged BLE/LoRaWAN tag with accelerometer (lift-cycle counter) on each hoist, cellular gateway; live ward location, 'exam due in 30 days' list for the inspector's visit, usage-based service alerts
notes: c4 (LOLER 6-monthly statutory exam), c6 (insurer engineering inspectors like Allianz/Zurich/HSB already visit every site), c2 (6-monthly cycle per item); c1 needs revisit-cost evidence

title: GP-to-lab pathology boxes cook in courier vans: rejected samples and repeat bleeds
problem: Blood samples ride for hours in courier vans; heat or cold exposure causes haemolysis and spurious potassium results, so samples are rejected or wrongly reported and patients recalled. ISO 15189 (UKAS) requires labs to control and monitor pre-examination transport conditions, but courier contracts give no temperature proof.
who_suffers: Lab quality managers, GP practices recalling patients, couriers blamed without data
buyer: Pathology Quality Manager / Pathology Logistics Manager
industry: Hospital pathology networks and GP specimen courier routes
current_workaround: Occasional validation runs with data loggers, courier SLAs, sample rejection on arrival
sensor_concept: Temperature logger + GNSS in each transport box, LTE-M, auto check-in on arrival at lab; per-route excursion report linked to rejected-sample rates
notes: c4 (ISO 15189 + UKAS audits), c2 (daily routes), c6 (pathology couriers/transport-box suppliers); c1 needs repeat-test cost sourcing

title: Towed passenger steps, baggage carts and ULD dollies strike aircraft with no data trail
problem: IATA puts aircraft ground damage at ~$5bn/yr, rising to ~$10bn by 2035, with belt-loaders, cargo loaders, passenger stairs and bridges ~40% of incidents; a single fuselage dent can ground an aircraft. Motorised GSE increasingly has telematics, but towed and non-powered stairs, carts and dollies have no power and no data, so strikes go unreported or unattributed.
who_suffers: Ground handlers and airlines paying AOG and repair costs; ramp safety managers
buyer: Ground Handling Safety Manager / Head of Ground Operations at the handler
industry: Airport ground handling of non-powered GSE
current_workaround: Walkround inspections before departure, voluntary occurrence reporting, CCTV review after damage found
sensor_concept: Rugged shock + GNSS tag on bumpers of towed GSE, LTE-M, multi-year battery; impacts above threshold inside a stand geofence trigger an instant damage-inspection alert and an evidence record
notes: c1 (IATA cost data), c4 (EU/UK 376/2014 occurrence reporting, ISAGO), c7 (gap: telematics only on powered GSE), c6 (GSE pools/lessors and maintenance providers)

title: Tow-bar oversteer and jerk loads crack nose landing gear; damage found later, blame disputed
problem: Conventional tow-bars push and pull aircraft; exceeding steering limits or shock loads from tug jerks has damaged nose gear (AAIB/NTSB cases include fractured drag braces and gear-door strikes). Damage is often found later and attribution between airline, tug driver and handler is disputed; shear pins break with no record.
who_suffers: Pushback crews, airline engineering, handler insurers
buyer: Head of Ground Operations / GSE Maintenance Manager at the handler
industry: Airport pushback and aircraft towing with conventional tow-bars
current_workaround: Shear pins, aircraft oversteer indicators where fitted, post-event inspections, manual tow-bar inspections
sensor_concept: IMU (accelerometer + gyro) on the tow-bar head logging steering angle and jerk events, LTE-M; per-tow record with stand and time, exceedance alerts, usage counts for tow-bar maintenance
notes: c1 (gear repair + AOG), c2 (every tow), c4 (occurrence reporting); c1/c10 need sourced repair costs

title: Fixed ground power and pre-conditioned air billed per 15 minutes, but older stands rely on manual logs
problem: Airports bill airlines for fixed 400Hz ground power and PCA by time (e.g. Athens ~€38.67 per 15 min) or per turn; on older stands usage is recorded manually by dispatchers or not metered, causing under-billing and disputes, and units left running after departure waste energy.
who_suffers: Airport revenue teams, dispatchers filling in logs, airlines disputing invoices
buyer: Aeronautical Revenue Manager / Airfield Engineering Manager
industry: Airport stand fixed electrical ground power and PCA
current_workaround: Dispatcher paper/app logs, flat per-turn fees, vendor-integrated billing only on new installations
sensor_concept: Clamp-on CTs on GPU/PCA output feeders per stand, LTE-M; automatic on/off times per turn reconciled to the flight schedule; idle-on alerts after departure
notes: c1 (revenue leakage per stand), c2 (every turn), c3 (manual logs), c7 (vendors only on new installs); c4 weak

title: Regional airport runs short of de-icing fluid in a cold snap and departures stop
problem: When Type I/II/IV de-icing fluid runs low during a freeze, departures are delayed or cancelled (UK261/EU261 compensation ~£220-£520/€250-600 per passenger plus disruption); handlers dip tanks by hand and suppliers deliver reactively.
who_suffers: De-icing crews, handlers and airlines facing delays
buyer: De-icing Manager / Head of Ground Operations at a regional airport or handler
industry: Regional airport aircraft de-icing fluid storage
current_workaround: Manual tank dips, phone orders, safety stock over-ordering
sensor_concept: Radar/ultrasonic level sensors on glycol storage tanks and de-icing rig tanks, LTE-M; supplier VMI auto-reorder, usage per aircraft for re-billing, low-stock alerts
notes: c6 (fluid suppliers deliver and could fund telemetry like oil distributors), c1 (delay costs), c2 (daily in winter); c7 risk — tank level sensing is commoditised elsewhere

title: Electric baggage tractors' lead-acid batteries killed by missed watering and deep discharge
problem: Traction batteries (~£5-10k each) on electric tugs and belt-loaders fail early from missed watering, deep discharge and opportunity-charging abuse; warranty claims are rejected without data and handlers run short of tugs at peak.
who_suffers: GSE workshop teams and shift managers short of tugs
buyer: GSE Fleet / Maintenance Manager
industry: Airport electric GSE fleets on lead-acid traction batteries
current_workaround: Manual watering rounds, hydrometer checks, reactive battery replacement
sensor_concept: Battery monitor with voltage, Hall-effect current, temperature and electrolyte-level probe, LTE-M or BLE-to-gateway; watering and abuse alerts, state-of-health and warranty evidence
notes: c1 (battery cost), c2 (daily cycles), c3 (manual watering), c6 (traction battery service engineers); c7 risk — forklift battery monitors exist, lithium GSE has built-in BMS

title: Remote airside crash gates found unsecured by security patrols or DfT inspectors
problem: Regional airports have many remote perimeter and crash gates; aviation security directions require them to be secured and checked, so officers patrol to test padlocks and chains. An unsecured gate found by DfT compliance inspectors means enforcement, and intrusions (e.g. protester incursions) close runways.
who_suffers: Airport security officers on patrol; operations when runways close
buyer: Head of Security / Aviation Security Manager
industry: UK regional and mid-size airport perimeter security
current_workaround: Vehicle patrols with checklists, padlock seals, CCTV on some gates
sensor_concept: Gate-closed magnetic sensor + padlock/chain tamper loop + vibration (climb/cut) sensor, solar/battery, LTE-M or LoRaWAN; open/tamper alerts to security control, automated patrol-equivalent log
notes: c4 (DfT aviation security directions + inspections), c2 (daily patrols), c3; c1 weak-moderate

title: Passengers' powered wheelchairs damaged in the hold; airline, handler and airport can't say where
problem: Powered wheelchairs (~£10-30k each) are regularly damaged in baggage handling; the UK CAA has pressed airlines on liability, and airlines, handlers and airports (responsible for PRM assistance under Reg 1107/2006) dispute where damage happened.
who_suffers: Disabled passengers left without mobility; airline customer-relations and claims teams
buyer: Airline Head of Accessibility / PRM service provider contract manager at the airport
industry: Airport PRM assistance and hold baggage handling of mobility aids
current_workaround: Pre-flight photos and tags, manual condition checks, claims settled after the fact
sensor_concept: Reusable strap-on shock + tilt + GNSS logger fitted at check-in and removed at arrival, LTE-M; records drops, tip-overs (battery orientation) and location by handling stage; damage evidence report
notes: c1 (high-value items, frequent claims), c4 (Reg 1107/2006 + Montreal Convention), c10 (public complaints); c5/c6 channel via PRM providers (OCS, Wilson James)

title: Baggage conveyor gearmotor fails at peak and hundreds of bags miss flights
problem: Baggage handling systems run thousands of gearmotors; an unexpected failure at peak leaves bags behind and each mishandled bag costs airlines ~$100+ to reunite (SITA). O&M contractors still rely on walkround inspections and run-to-failure for most drives.
who_suffers: BHS maintenance technicians, airline baggage services, passengers
buyer: BHS Maintenance Manager (airport or O&M contractor)
industry: Airport baggage handling systems (conveyor and sorter drives)
current_workaround: Scheduled walkrounds, vibration pens on critical drives, reactive repair
sensor_concept: Magnet-mount triaxial vibration + temperature sensor on each gearmotor, LoRaWAN to cellular gateway; trend-based failure warnings and maintenance work orders
notes: c1 (mishandled bag costs), c2 (continuous), c6 (BHS O&M contractors like Vanderlande/Alstef service teams); c7 risk — industrial condition monitoring exists at £200+/point

title: HMO weekly fire alarm tests skipped or unrecorded: civil penalties up to £30k per offence
problem: HMO managers must keep fire alarms working under the HMO Management Regulations 2006 and councils expect weekly tests and records (LACORS/BS 5839-6); councils issue civil penalties up to £30k per offence and fines (e.g. Gateshead ~£42k including missing checks/records, Liverpool ~£20k). Agents either drive to each HMO weekly or rely on tenants, and panel fault LEDs go unnoticed.
who_suffers: HMO letting agents and landlords; tenants exposed to dead alarms
buyer: HMO letting agency Compliance/Portfolio Manager
industry: Licensed HMOs managed by letting agents (England)
current_workaround: Weekly site visits or tenant-signed test logbooks; 6-monthly alarm servicing by contractors
sensor_concept: Box near the alarm panel with a sounder-detecting microphone and photodiodes on fault/power LEDs, battery or mains with backup, LTE-M; auto weekly test record when a call point is tested, fault/silenced/power-loss alerts, licence-renewal evidence pack
notes: Strong c4 (statutory + civil penalties), c1 (sourced fines), c2 (weekly), c6 (fire alarm maintainers and HMO agents)

title: Thieves strip brass dry riser landing valves and the whole riser fails until the next inspection
problem: Brass dry riser valves (~£270 each) are stolen from tower blocks for scrap (Aberdeen lost 32 valves across two blocks, Bristol 11 blocks in a month); one missing valve disables the riser for firefighters. Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022 require monthly checks of firefighting equipment in high-rise blocks and reporting faults to the fire service.
who_suffers: Residents and firefighters; building safety teams discovering thefts late
buyer: Building Safety Manager / Head of Fire Safety at council or housing association
industry: Social housing high-rise blocks with dry/wet risers
current_workaround: Monthly/6-monthly visual inspections, valve marking, locked boxes, patrols; PTSG sells anti-theft protection
sensor_concept: Tamper/vibration + tilt tag on each landing valve (or wire loop through the handwheel) and door contact on inlet/landing boxes; LoRaWAN with cellular gateway in the riser; instant theft alert and monthly check record
notes: c4 (FS(E)R 2022 monthly checks), c1 (valve and system cost), c6 (riser test contractors, PTSG already sells anti-theft = WTP), c10 (news + council warnings)

title: Void council homes: insurer demands 7-day inspections and drain-down proof or the escape-of-water claim is refused
problem: Insurer unoccupancy conditions typically require internal and external inspections at least every 7 days, water drained or heating held at ~5-10°C, and logs kept 12 months; breach voids escape-of-water and malicious damage cover. Social landlords with hundreds of voids pay security firms for screens and weekly inspections, and still get burst pipes and break-ins.
who_suffers: Voids teams, insurance managers, incoming tenants delayed
buyer: Voids Manager / Asset Manager at housing association or council
industry: Social housing and PRS void (empty) properties
current_workaround: Steel screens and alarms rented from void security firms, weekly paid inspections, drain-downs
sensor_concept: Plug-in hub with battery backup: temperature, leak rope, PIR/door, screen-removal vibration and mains-loss detect, LTE-M; automated 'inspection-equivalent' weekly report for the insurer, heating-threshold proof, intrusion and leak alerts
notes: c4 (insurer conditions), c2 (weekly), c3 (paid inspections), c6 (void security firms and brokers); c7 risk — void alarm rentals exist, gap is insurer-accepted remote inspection

title: Heat network residents without heating for days; Ofgem now regulates outages and compensation
problem: Residents on communal heat networks (many in social housing) lose heating/hot water when HIUs fail, and operators often learn only from complaints. Ofgem began regulating heat networks on 27 Jan 2026, with outage compensation (consultation proposed ~£45/day per unplanned interruption) and Guaranteed Standards expected from ~2027, so operators need outage start/stop evidence; poor HIU return temperatures also waste energy.
who_suffers: Residents, housing association heat network teams, operators facing compensation
buyer: Heat Network Manager / Head of Energy Services at housing association
industry: Communal and district heat networks in social housing blocks
current_workaround: Complaint-driven call-outs, annual HIU servicing, heat-meter reads for billing only
sensor_concept: Clamp-on pipe temperature sensors on HIU primary flow/return and DHW outlet, battery NB-IoT/LoRaWAN; no-heat/valve-stuck/high-return alerts, outage timestamps for compensation and regulatory reporting
notes: c4 (new Ofgem regime), c1 (compensation + energy waste), c2 (daily), c6 (metering/billing and O&M firms like Insite, SAV, Switch2); risk: proposed not-for-profit landlord exemption

title: Tower-block cold-water booster set fails and upper floors lose water overnight
problem: Booster pump sets in blocks fail (seized pump, lost vessel charge, controller trip) and residents above a certain floor lose water; landlords pay emergency call-outs, bottled water deliveries and compensation. Contractors visit only quarterly or annually and older sets have no remote alarm.
who_suffers: Residents (often vulnerable), housing repairs teams
buyer: M&E / Building Services Manager at housing association or council
industry: Social housing medium/high-rise blocks with boosted cold water
current_workaround: PPM visits, resident phone reports, out-of-hours emergency call-outs
sensor_concept: Pressure transducer on the delivery manifold + CT clamps on pump motors (short-cycling = vessel failure), LTE-M; failure and pre-failure alerts, uptime log for the PPM contractor
notes: c1 (emergency costs, compensation), c3 (PPM visits), c6 (pump maintenance contractors); c4 moderate (HHSRS/Decent Homes, Housing Ombudsman)

title: Unadopted sewage pumping station on a housing estate fails and sewage backs up into homes
problem: Private pumping stations serving housing association estates block with wipes or lose a float switch; sewage backs into homes and gardens or overflows to watercourses (EA pollution offences), remediation runs ~£10k+ per affected home, and Housing Ombudsman cases show months-long failures. Many have only a local beacon nobody sees.
who_suffers: Residents, housing association asset teams, the environment
buyer: Asset / Estates Manager at housing association; estate management companies
industry: Unadopted sewage pumping stations on social and new-build estates
current_workaround: 6-monthly contractor service, resident reports, local beacon alarms
sensor_concept: Hydrostatic/ultrasonic wet-well level sensor + pump current clamps, LTE-M with battery backup; high-level, pump-fail and run-hour alerts to the contractor
notes: c1 (flooding remediation), c4 (EA pollution + Housing Ombudsman), c6 (pumping station service contractors), c7 (telemetry outstations cost ~£1-3k)

title: Package sewage treatment plant blower dies on a rural housing scheme; septic discharge breaches General Binding Rules
problem: Rural housing association schemes off mains drainage use small package treatment plants; if the air blower fails the plant turns septic and discharges poor effluent to a watercourse, breaching EA General Binding Rules (maintain to manufacturer spec, keep records), risking enforcement and pollution clean-up.
who_suffers: Rural housing teams, neighbours, local watercourses
buyer: Compliance Manager / Asset Manager at rural housing association
industry: Package sewage treatment plants serving rural social housing
current_workaround: Annual service and desludging visits, resident smell complaints
sensor_concept: Air-pressure sensor in the diffuser line + blower current clamp + final-chamber level sensor, NB-IoT/LTE-M; blower-fail and high-level alerts, service and desludge records for GBR compliance
notes: c4 (EA GBR + enforcement), c6 (PTP service/desludge contractors), c2; distinct from pumping stations (treatment process, air pressure)

title: Retrofit air source heat pumps quietly fall back to immersion and tenants' bills explode — no Wi-Fi to monitor them
problem: Thousands of ASHPs installed under SHDF/ECO in social homes; when they fault or default to the immersion heater, tenants face high bills and complain (Housing Ombudsman cases about ASHP running costs), and landlords have no performance data because manufacturer cloud monitoring needs tenant Wi-Fi that is often absent or disconnected.
who_suffers: Tenants in fuel poverty; housing sustainability and repairs teams
buyer: Sustainability / Asset Manager at housing association or council
industry: Social housing air source heat pump retrofits
current_workaround: Annual service visits, tenant complaints, bill analysis on request
sensor_concept: CT clamps on the heat-pump supply and immersion circuits + flow/return pipe temperatures, LTE-M (no tenant Wi-Fi); estimated COP, immersion-fallback and fault alerts, portfolio performance report
notes: c1 (tenant bills/complaints), c2 (continuous), c6 (MCS installers doing annual service), c8 (no customer IT); c4 moderate

title: Tower-block refuse chutes block daily; bags pile on landings and chute fires start
problem: Refuse chutes in high-rise blocks block regularly; residents leave bags on landings (fire load in escape routes) and chute fires occur, while hopper doors that fail to close spread smoke. Caretakers inspect and clear chutes daily.
who_suffers: Caretakers, residents, building safety teams
buyer: Estate Services / Caretaking Manager; Building Safety Manager
industry: Social housing high-rise blocks with refuse chutes
current_workaround: Daily caretaker rounds, rodding, chute cleaning contractors, resident complaints
sensor_concept: Time-of-flight distance sensor looking up the chute from the bin room (fill-up/blockage), heat-rise sensor at the chute base, hopper door contacts; LoRaWAN/LTE-M; blockage and fire-risk alerts with caretaker round log
notes: c2 (daily), c3 (caretaker labour), c4 (FSO/FS(E)R escape-route duties); c1 needs fire/clean-up cost sourcing

title: Monthly emergency lighting flick tests in small blocks cost a contractor visit each time
problem: BS 5266-1 requires monthly functional tests and an annual full-duration test of emergency lighting with records, enforced under the Fire Safety Order; managing agents and housing associations with hundreds of small low-rise blocks pay contractors per visit (~£50-100, to verify) just to turn a test key and log results.
who_suffers: Block managing agents and compliance teams; contractors driving round
buyer: Compliance Manager at managing agent or housing association
industry: Low/mid-rise residential blocks' communal emergency lighting
current_workaround: Monthly contractor or caretaker flick tests with paper logbooks; costly self-test luminaire retrofits
sensor_concept: Retrofit relay on the existing test key-switch circuit plus stick-on photodiode tags on each emergency fitting, LoRaWAN/LTE-M; remotely triggered monthly/annual tests with automatic pass/fail log per fitting
notes: c2 (monthly mandated test), c3 (paid visits), c4 (BS 5266 + FSO), c6 (fire/electrical contractors); c8 needs an electrician for the relay

title: Big-cat keeper doors and slides left open: keeper deaths and six-figure fines
problem: Keepers have been killed when a slide or keeper door was left open (South Lakes Safari Zoo fined ~£255k after Sarah McClay's death; Rosa King killed at Hamerton Zoo Park in 2017); zoos rely on paper lock-check sign-offs every shift, and licensing inspectors review key and door procedures.
who_suffers: Keepers working dangerous-animal sections; curators and zoo directors
buyer: Head of Animal Operations / Zoo Curator / H&S Manager
industry: UK licensed zoos and safari parks with Category 1 (dangerous) animals
current_workaround: Two-person lock checks, padlocks and tags, paper sign-off sheets, CCTV
sensor_concept: Reed/hall door-position sensors on keeper doors and animal slides + padlock-closed detection, LoRaWAN with cellular gateway; tablet status board per house, advisory alarm when keeper-side and animal-side are open together, time-stamped lock-check log (advisory, not a safety interlock)
notes: Strong c1 + c4 (sourced HSE fines, HSWA + Zoo Licensing Act), c2 (every shift), c10 (press + inquests); c6 needs a zoo engineering/insurer channel

title: Hot-wire fence on a primate or carnivore enclosure shorts on wet vegetation and animals learn to test it
problem: Many enclosures use electric fencing as a secondary barrier; vegetation, snow or a broken insulator drops voltage and animals escape. Escapes must be reported to the licensing authority within 24h and trigger inspection scrutiny, recapture costs and sometimes animal destruction; keepers check fences daily with a hand tester and record readings.
who_suffers: Keepers doing daily fence checks; curators answering to inspectors
buyer: Head of Animal Operations / Facilities Manager
industry: Zoos and wildlife parks using electric fencing on enclosures
current_workaround: Daily hand-tester readings on paper, vegetation clearance, energiser alarms on some units
sensor_concept: HV pulse-voltage divider monitor per fence zone, LoRaWAN, battery/solar; alerts when voltage drops, automatic daily record per zone
notes: c2 (daily checks), c4 (licence conditions on barrier maintenance and escape reporting), c6 (electric fencing dealers); c7 risk — agricultural fence monitors exist

title: Aquarium life-support pump trips overnight and an entire exhibit suffocates
problem: Pump or electrical failures overnight have killed whole exhibits: ~54 rays at Brookfield Zoo; 18 stingrays and 3 sharks at John Ball Zoo after a pump failed and the backup alert didn't fire; 200+ fish at the National Marine Aquarium after a power loss. Smaller UK aquaria and zoo aquarium houses rely on keeper rounds and local alarms.
who_suffers: Aquarists, curators, animals; visitor income when exhibits close
buyer: Aquarium Curator / Life Support Systems Manager
industry: Public aquaria, zoo aquarium houses, penguin and sea lion pools
current_workaround: Keeper rounds, local alarm beacons, hobby-grade controllers on Wi-Fi, SCADA only at large aquaria
sensor_concept: CT clamps on LSS pumps/blowers + sump float/ultrasonic level + water temperature + mains-loss detection, LTE-M with battery backup; phone-call escalation alarms and daily LSS log
notes: c1 (sourced mass-mortality events), c2 (daily checks), c8 (cellular, no IT), c7 (gap between Wi-Fi hobby controllers and SCADA)

title: Vivarium and tropical-house heating fails on a winter night and breeding-programme amphibians and reptiles die
problem: A failed thermostat, heater or heat lamp on a cold night can kill temperature-dependent collections such as endangered amphibians in breeding programmes, reptiles and butterfly-house stock; keepers record temperatures manually twice a day and the Zoo Licensing standards require suitable environments and records.
who_suffers: Herpetology/invertebrate keepers; conservation breeding programmes
buyer: Curator (Reptiles & Amphibians) / Head of Animal Operations
industry: Zoo reptile houses, amphibian conservation units and tropical/butterfly houses
current_workaround: Twice-daily manual thermometer readings, thermostats with no remote alarm, night checks at larger zoos
sensor_concept: Multi-point temperature/RH probes per vivarium or zone + heater current clamps, LoRaWAN with cellular gateway; out-of-range alarms and automatic environmental records for inspections
notes: c2 (twice-daily records), c4 (licensing standards), c7 (gap for multi-vivarium alerting without IT); c1 needs animal-value sourcing

title: Automatic animal drinkers freeze or jam in paddocks and houses; keepers check every one daily
problem: Zoo standards require animals to have constant access to clean water; automatic drinkers freeze in winter or jam (leaving animals dry) or overflow (flooding houses and running up water bills). Keepers check each drinker on every round.
who_suffers: Hoofstock and primate keepers; animals
buyer: Head of Animal Operations / Facilities Manager
industry: Zoos and wildlife parks with automatic drinkers in paddocks and houses
current_workaround: Daily visual checks, trace heating on some lines, manual buckets in freezes
sensor_concept: Inline flow pulse sensor + water temperature (freeze) on each drinker feed, LoRaWAN; no-flow and freeze alerts, overflow detection
notes: c2 (daily rounds), c4 (welfare standards on water access); c1 weak — overlaps livestock trough monitors

title: Storm drops a tree on the perimeter fence overnight; staff walk kilometres of fence at dawn
problem: Licensed zoos must keep a sound perimeter fence to prevent escapes and intruders; storms bring trees down on fences overnight and intruders have stolen animals from UK zoos. Staff patrol the full perimeter daily and after every storm, which can be several km at safari and wildlife parks.
who_suffers: Grounds and security staff, keepers, management facing escape risk
buyer: Head of Facilities / Operations Manager
industry: Safari parks, wildlife parks and large zoos with long perimeters
current_workaround: Daily perimeter walks or drives, post-storm inspections, CCTV at gates
sensor_concept: Tilt + vibration nodes on fence posts every ~50 m, LoRaWAN with solar gateway; lean/impact alerts with location, automated patrol log
notes: c4 (zoo licensing perimeter fence standard), c2 (daily patrols), c3 (patrol labour); c1 weak

title: Misting and fogging systems in tropical and reptile houses are an unmanaged Legionella source
problem: Misting and fogging systems that create humidity in tropical, reptile and butterfly houses spray aerosols over visitors and staff; HSE's HSG274 Part 3 covers such systems and requires risk assessment, temperature/stagnation control and records. Misting devices have been linked to Legionnaires' outbreaks elsewhere, and HSE has prosecuted operators of aerosol-generating systems.
who_suffers: Facilities teams, visitors, keepers
buyer: Facilities / H&S Manager at the zoo
industry: Zoo tropical, reptile and butterfly houses with misting/fogging systems
current_workaround: Annual L8 risk assessment by water hygiene contractor, ad-hoc cleaning, rarely any temperature monitoring
sensor_concept: Temperature probes on mister reservoir and supply line + pump current (run/stagnation detection), LoRaWAN; alerts for water above 20°C or not run for N days, auto records for the L8 logbook
notes: c4 (L8 ACOP/HSG274 + HSE enforcement), c2 (weekly checks), c6 (water hygiene contractors already visit zoos); c1 needs sourcing

title: Petting-farm handwash stations run out of soap or hot water and an E. coli O157 outbreak follows
problem: Open farms and zoo contact areas must provide working handwashing for visitors (HSE guidance and the industry code of practice on ill health from animal contact); the 2009 Godstone Farm E. coli O157 outbreak made 93 people ill and led to the Griffin review. Staff check soap, water and hot water at outdoor stations through the day, and failures are common inspection findings.
who_suffers: Visitors (especially children), farm operators facing closure and claims
buyer: Operations Manager / H&S Manager at zoo-licensed open farm or zoo
industry: Zoo-licensed open farms and petting/contact areas
current_workaround: Staff checks during the day, paper cleaning logs, signage
sensor_concept: Soap-reservoir level (IR/weight) + water flow/usage counter + hot-water temperature at each outdoor handwash station, LoRaWAN; empty/no-hot-water alerts, usage vs visitor count report as compliance evidence
notes: c4 (HSE guidance + code of practice), c1 (outbreak costs, claims), c10 (public inquiry); c2 daily; c7 likely no niche product

title: Visitors leave both doors of walk-through aviaries and lemur exhibits open and animals escape
problem: Walk-through exhibits (aviaries, lemur and wallaby walk-throughs, butterfly houses) use double-door airlocks; visitors prop or hold both doors and animals escape, risking loss of valuable birds/primates, licence escape reports within 24h and recapture work.
who_suffers: Keepers and rangers stationed at doors, curators
buyer: Head of Animal Operations / Visitor Operations Manager
industry: Zoo and wildlife park walk-through exhibits
current_workaround: Staff stationed at doors at peak times, signage, spring closers
sensor_concept: Door contacts on both airlock doors with a local buzzer when both are open plus LoRaWAN alerts and a daily breach count
notes: c2 (daily), c4 (escape reporting); c1 weak; cheap and simple (c8)
